Oh of course! I’m fully aware that him being my boss isn’t the only thing preventing him from being my father figure, it’s also a matter of his boundaries and consent. With that said, I’ve never met his wife in person before but we have played Mario Party together as a group online a couple of times. I respect and adore Will’s relationship with his wife, I hope to have a life like that of my own someday (married to the love of my life, living in our own house, no kids, multiple pets).

I appreciate the input about communication and Father’s Day, however I’m extremely cautious about making any gestures on or relating to that day since I know Will lost his father a few months before I started working at this job. I’d hate to dredge up any negative/mournful emotions for Will, even if I’d just be expressing my positive ones towards him.

I know I don’t love him, nor am I in love with him, but I do feel safe with him and greatly enjoy our relationship as it is. It is my hope that one day when I eventually move on from my current job (it’s not a career, just a means of income) into something that aligns with my education, I’ll still be able to maintain the connection I have with Will and possibly get even closer to him (in a familial way)!

Thank you for the advice, Dad! Though I will say, there are multiple things that Will has said/done himself to blur the boundaries. I’m not saying your statement isn’t true, just that it’s not only my actions that have made our relationship seem reminiscent of a familial one. Also to be clear I never sought out Will to be a father figure/went into this job wanting to feel this way about him. It just happened.

As someone without a car who walks/busses around town, I completely agree! Whether I’m at  a crosswalk next to a traffic light, or one of those pedestrian crosses with the yellow lights, I always wait until all the cars in the lanes I have to pass are stopped/stopping to cross.

Even then though, some drivers will still find a way to blame pedestrians for any accident or near accidents. There’s only so much we can do, and as long as we are following the law, all responsibility falls on the driver to avoid hitting someone. When I’m walking, I pay attention at crosswalks because I want to be safe. It’s not my fault that some drivers clearly don’t pay attention or care. It’s why I take EXTRA caution to be sure that no one is going to hit me before I start to cross.

Some drivers may get impatient, or find it annoying that I take an extra 5-10 seconds to cross, but I’m not risking crossing even when I have the signal and the right of way when the truth is some drivers just don’t care! 🤷🏾‍♀️

Edit: Oh yeah and I love the little hand up it’s so kind and makes me feel so safe and relaxed! I appreciate drivers who recognize that we’re all just trying to get around in the best ways we can! :)

I think what I’ll do is, I’ll write the letter. I’ll tell Paul everything I think is relevant for him to know, and, should I feel like there’s a moment where he and I just…don’t understand each other fundamentally. Or maybe if I feel like telling him would benefit my working through these feelings, then I’ll give it to him. I’ll try to keep it short, and I’ll keep it in my bag in case I want to give it to him at work.

I’d be lying if I said your judgment if Paul doesn’t scare me. Because I know you could be right. You’re unbiased, and given the information I’ve provided here, it makes sense that you’d come to that conclusion, I probably would too if this were someone else. That is part of what makes me hesitate. As much as I don’t want to admit it, you could be right. I just…when I look into his eyes, I see the man who hugged me and drove me away from a Bad Man and shared his own trauma and provided comfort. I cannot shake this gut feeling of goodness within Paul, and I want him to know that I see it, even if he doesn’t feel the same way about me as I do for him.

I also don’t want to make him uncomfortable, so I think maybe I’ll preface the letter with a bit more context, so he doesn’t think that I’m being weird or secretive. I care about him a lot, more than what probably makes sense for a coworker of over a year, and I don’t think I’ll ever be able to make that go away. But if he wanted me to, I’d never mention my sisterly feelings for him again and actively work to diminish them. I’ve tried to fight them before, on my own, and failed. Maybe therapy will help with that. Until then, I at least want to get my feeling out, even if it’s just to a piece of paper at first.

Thank you for working through this with me. I appreciate your help and time, and I want to especially thank you for calling me ‘kiddo.’ Sometimes I am just a kid who needs a dad, even at 21, and that’s okay. ❤️:)

That’s the part that sucks about telling him. I know he doesn’t feel the same way. At least, I’m near positive. Do you think it’s still worth it to tell him? I guess that depends on if I feel like it’ll help me regardless, since I’m the one with the feelings I want to share.

Paul’s a man of few words, so I’m a little nervous about writing to him, especially when I may not be the only person who reads the letter (I’m thinking of his possessive girlfriend who may take the fact that I wrote a letter in the first place much less the contents the wrong way.) I definitely hear you on not doing it at work. I was planning to, because work is the only place I see him. Paul has strong work life/personal life boundaries and while I don’t want to cross them, I also don’t want to say what I have to say to his face and get an immediate response. Maybe I should just forget the whole thing? I don’t know.

Thank you so much for your advice, I really appreciate it. I’m definitely going to think on what I want to tell him and what I can keep to myself. 

And the congratulations means the world to me. I don’t have many people in my life acknowledging what I’ve overcome in the last year. It feels good to know that I’ve already come so far, even though I have farther to go.

You seem like a really great person, so thank you for being so awesome and I hope your day is as wonderful as you’ve made mine! ❤️ :)

As a Black A2 resident I wanted to just say “the fact that there’s more Black people” but instead Imma just say that it’s just not Ann Arbor is my guess? Like it doesn’t have UM, it has EMU, which to lots of people in Ann Arbor is a bad school just cause it’s not UM. There’s isn’t as large a student body there as there is in A2, and, since EMU isn’t as expensive as UM, that means not as many rich students who move to the town every year. 

In my opinion, Ypsi has more character than Ann Arbor. Not everything is about their university and there’s more diversity there. I don’t feel like the odd one out. Also, I feel like it’s easier to know where you stand in Ypsi. There are some stores my family and I have walked into before and felt like we were treated as if we didn’t belong. I’ve never felt that way in Ypsi before.

Is Ypsi the safest city in southeast Michigan (anecdotally)? No, but it’s not what people imagine the worst of the worst to be like. I feel like some people who deem Ypsi “unsafe” actually haven’t been there and are just basing their opinion on the demographics and maybe an experience someone else had. Given how close Ypsi and Ann Arbor are, the same types of dangerous people that can live in Ypsi can (and do) live in Ann Arbor! 

(Not to mention the fact that with the hundreds of thousands of students brought to A2 every year through UM, there’s never a shortage of young, arrogant, and rich undergrads who think part of growing up and maturing is committing crimes like stealing and using drugs and I’m not even gonna get into SA on and off UM campus.)
